records.title: What Is Chain of Custody? A Guide for Ediscovery Teams
records.retrieval_query: What is the chain of custody for the laptop, including who transferred it and when, according to available records?
records.visible_text:
Reading Time — 8 minutes

March 26, 2026

Chain of custody, in the simplest of terms, is the chronological, documented record of everyone who has handled, accessed, or stored a piece of evidence. It serves as a “paper trail” that tracks the journey from the moment evidence is collected until it is presented in a legal proceeding. The purpose is to prove it has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

Such documentation is important to establish trust that the evidence is authentic and therefore admissible in court. The Federal Rules of Evidence govern the admissibility and authentication of evidence. Proper chain of custody helps convince the court there is a reasonable probability that the evidence is what the party claims it is, and is in substantially the same condition as when it was collected.

Without documentation showing who collected the evidence, when and where, who handled or accessed it, and how it was stored or transferred, opposing counsel may argue that it is unreliable or inadmissible, which can jeopardize the case.

Chain of custody documentation is a best practice for the handling of both physical and digital evidence.

## Key Takeaways for Legal Teams

* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.
* Courts evaluate custody to assess whether evidence was managed in a reasonably reliable and defensible manner, not whether handling was perfect.
* Breakdowns in the chain of custody can lead to admissibility challenges, adverse inference instructions, monetary sanctions, or other remedial measures.
* In ediscovery, consistency, traceability, and auditability are critical because if digital data is improperly duplicated, modified, or moved, it becomes harder to validate its authenticity.
* Defensible chain of custody is critical during discovery planning, where parties define how evidence will be handled so the approach can later be explained and justified.
* Strong custody practices allow legal teams to focus on substantive arguments rather than defending their processes under scrutiny.

## What Does Chain of Custody Mean in Legal Contexts?

In the legal context, chain of custody is defined as the “chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical or electronic evidence.” This type of record helps establish that evidence is authentic, reliable, and substantially unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

Traditionally associated with physical evidence, chain of custody today applies equally to digital information. Proper documentation shows there were controls and safeguards in place continuously against alteration or loss of evidence. The documentation typically covers who had access, when, how it was stored, and how it moved between custodians or systems.

Modern custody of the evidence practices emphasize accountability, not just possession. Documentation that shows what controls were in place — such as locked storage for physical evidence or audit trails for electronic evidence — and whether handling procedures met reasonable standards helps establish integrity and allows a party to respond to tampering or contamination challenges. For electronic evidence, this may include controls around access permissions, audit trails, preservation measures, and defensible workflows that demonstrate responsible handling.

# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

S2:P12:P18.literal_quote:
Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

\_\_\_\_\_  
  
**Editor's note:** *The Associated Press contributed to this article.*

Reading Time — 8 minutes

March 26, 2026

Chain of custody, in the simplest of terms, is the chronological, documented record of everyone who has handled, accessed, or stored a piece of evidence. It serves as a “paper trail” that tracks the journey from the moment evidence is collected until it is presented in a legal proceeding. The purpose is to prove it has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

Such documentation is important to establish trust that the evidence is authentic and therefore admissible in court. The Federal Rules of Evidence govern the admissibility and authentication of evidence. Proper chain of custody helps convince the court there is a reasonable probability that the evidence is what the party claims it is, and is in substantially the same condition as when it was collected.

Without documentation showing who collected the evidence, when and where, who handled or accessed it, and how it was stored or transferred, opposing counsel may argue that it is unreliable or inadmissible, which can jeopardize the case.

Chain of custody documentation is a best practice for the handling of both physical and digital evidence.

## Key Takeaways for Legal Teams

S6:P8:P10.literal_quote:
* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.
* Courts evaluate custody to assess whether evidence was managed in a reasonably reliable and defensible manner, not whether handling was perfect.
* Breakdowns in the chain of custody can lead to admissibility challenges, adverse inference instructions, monetary sanctions, or other remedial measures.
* In ediscovery, consistency, traceability, and auditability are critical because if digital data is improperly duplicated, modified, or moved, it becomes harder to validate its authenticity.
* Defensible chain of custody is critical during discovery planning, where parties define how evidence will be handled so the approach can later be explained and justified.
* Strong custody practices allow legal teams to focus on substantive arguments rather than defending their processes under scrutiny.

## What Does Chain of Custody Mean in Legal Contexts?

In the legal context, chain of custody is defined as the “chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical or electronic evidence.” This type of record helps establish that evidence is authentic, reliable, and substantially unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

S6:P11:P12.literal_quote:
Traditionally associated with physical evidence, chain of custody today applies equally to digital information. Proper documentation shows there were controls and safeguards in place continuously against alteration or loss of evidence. The documentation typically covers who had access, when, how it was stored, and how it moved between custodians or systems.

Modern custody of the evidence practices emphasize accountability, not just possession. Documentation that shows what controls were in place — such as locked storage for physical evidence or audit trails for electronic evidence — and whether handling procedures met reasonable standards helps establish integrity and allows a party to respond to tampering or contamination challenges. For electronic evidence, this may include controls around access permissions, audit trails, preservation measures, and defensible workflows that demonstrate responsible handling.

S7:P1:P1.literal_quote: Chain of custody is the documented record of who collected, handled, transferred, examined, and stored evidence throughout an investigation.

U29.literal_quote:
# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

U30.literal_quote:
Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

Reading Time — 8 minutes

Chain of custody, in the simplest of terms, is the chronological, documented record of everyone who has handled, accessed, or stored a piece of evidence. It serves as a “paper trail” that tracks the journey from the moment evidence is collected until it is presented in a legal proceeding. The purpose is to prove it has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

Such documentation is important to establish trust that the evidence is authentic and therefore admissible in court. The Federal Rules of Evidence govern the admissibility and authentication of evidence. Proper chain of custody helps convince the court there is a reasonable probability that the evidence is what the party claims it is, and is in substantially the same condition as when it was collected.

Without documentation showing who collected the evidence, when and where, who handled or accessed it, and how it was stored or transferred, opposing counsel may argue that it is unreliable or inadmissible, which can jeopardize the case.

Chain of custody documentation is a best practice for the handling of both physical and digital evidence.

## Key Takeaways for Legal Teams

U47.literal_quote:
* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.
* Courts evaluate custody to assess whether evidence was managed in a reasonably reliable and defensible manner, not whether handling was perfect.
* Breakdowns in the chain of custody can lead to admissibility challenges, adverse inference instructions, monetary sanctions, or other remedial measures.
* In ediscovery, consistency, traceability, and auditability are critical because if digital data is improperly duplicated, modified, or moved, it becomes harder to validate its authenticity.
* Defensible chain of custody is critical during discovery planning, where parties define how evidence will be handled so the approach can later be explained and justified.
* Strong custody practices allow legal teams to focus on substantive arguments rather than defending their processes under scrutiny.

## What Does Chain of Custody Mean in Legal Contexts?

In the legal context, chain of custody is defined as the “chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical or electronic evidence.” This type of record helps establish that evidence is authentic, reliable, and substantially unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

U48.literal_quote:
Traditionally associated with physical evidence, chain of custody today applies equally to digital information. Proper documentation shows there were controls and safeguards in place continuously against alteration or loss of evidence. The documentation typically covers who had access, when, how it was stored, and how it moved between custodians or systems.

Modern custody of the evidence practices emphasize accountability, not just possession. Documentation that shows what controls were in place — such as locked storage for physical evidence or audit trails for electronic evidence — and whether handling procedures met reasonable standards helps establish integrity and allows a party to respond to tampering or contamination challenges. For electronic evidence, this may include controls around access permissions, audit trails, preservation measures, and defensible workflows that demonstrate responsible handling.

U49.literal_quote: Chain of custody is the documented record of who collected, handled, transferred, examined, and stored evidence throughout an investigation.

# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

\_\_\_\_\_  
  
**Editor's note:** *The Associated Press contributed to this article.*

At 5:00 a.m. ET, on Wednesday, October 14, 2020, less than three weeks before the 2020 
presidential election, the New York Post published a potentially election-altering news story 
about a years-long influence peddling scheme carried out by the family of the Democratic 
nominee for president, former Vice President Joe Biden.2 The Post article detailed how Hunter 
Biden leveraged his famous last name to provide foreign officials with access to his father in 
exchange for the Biden family’s significant financial gain.3 This information was recovered from 
the hard drive of a laptop attributed to Hunter Biden, and the article included pictures of a signed 
federal subpoena, demonstrating that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had seized that 
hard drive.4 Neither Hunter Biden nor the Biden presidential campaign denied the allegations or 
the provenance of the laptop; indeed, the Biden Department of Justice (DOJ) has since 
authenticated the laptop as evidence in federal court.5

The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION 
Interim Staff Report of the 
Committee on the Judiciary 
and the 
Select Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government 
U.S. House of Representatives 
October 30, 2024

1 
 
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 
 
“But, when we get hauled up to [Capitol] hill to testify on why we 
influenced the 2020 elections we can say we have been meeting for 
YEARS with USG [U.S. Government] to plan for it.” 
 
—July 15, 2020, 3:17 p.m. ET, internal Facebook message 
during Facebook’s meeting with the FBI and other agencies.1

authenticated the laptop as evidence in federal court.5

# Testimony Reveals FBI Employees Who Warned Social Media Companies about Hack and Leak Operation Knew Hunter Biden Laptop Wasn’t Russian Disinformation

July 20, 2023

Press Release

**WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.  
  
The *Post* published its story early in the morning on October 14. That same day, representatives from the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force attended a previously scheduled meeting with Twitter, during which a Twitter employee asked the FITF about the authenticity of laptop. According to Section Chief Dehmlow’s testimony, an analyst in the FBI’s Criminal Investigative Division embedded in FITF began to respond that the laptop was real, when an FBI lawyer interrupted to say that the FBI had “no further comment,” regarding the laptop’s provenance:

Image

Later on October 14, FITF met with Facebook. During the FITF-Facebook meeting, Dehmlow responded to a similar question from a Facebook employee about Hunter Biden’s laptop by stating that the FBI, again, had “no comment.” The FBI made this decision despite being in possession of the laptop and having confirmed its authenticity. According to Dehmlow, multiple personnel on FITF knew that the laptop was real. She testified:

Image

# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

\_\_\_\_\_  
  
**Editor's note:** *The Associated Press contributed to this article.*

records.title: What Is Chain of Custody? A Guide for Ediscovery Teams
records.retrieval_query: What is the chain of custody for the laptop, including who transferred it and when, according to available records?
records.visible_text:
Reading Time — 8 minutes

March 26, 2026

Chain of custody, in the simplest of terms, is the chronological, documented record of everyone who has handled, accessed, or stored a piece of evidence. It serves as a “paper trail” that tracks the journey from the moment evidence is collected until it is presented in a legal proceeding. The purpose is to prove it has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

Such documentation is important to establish trust that the evidence is authentic and therefore admissible in court. The Federal Rules of Evidence govern the admissibility and authentication of evidence. Proper chain of custody helps convince the court there is a reasonable probability that the evidence is what the party claims it is, and is in substantially the same condition as when it was collected.

Without documentation showing who collected the evidence, when and where, who handled or accessed it, and how it was stored or transferred, opposing counsel may argue that it is unreliable or inadmissible, which can jeopardize the case.

Chain of custody documentation is a best practice for the handling of both physical and digital evidence.

## Key Takeaways for Legal Teams

* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.
* Courts evaluate custody to assess whether evidence was managed in a reasonably reliable and defensible manner, not whether handling was perfect.
* Breakdowns in the chain of custody can lead to admissibility challenges, adverse inference instructions, monetary sanctions, or other remedial measures.
* In ediscovery, consistency, traceability, and auditability are critical because if digital data is improperly duplicated, modified, or moved, it becomes harder to validate its authenticity.
* Defensible chain of custody is critical during discovery planning, where parties define how evidence will be handled so the approach can later be explained and justified.
* Strong custody practices allow legal teams to focus on substantive arguments rather than defending their processes under scrutiny.

## What Does Chain of Custody Mean in Legal Contexts?

In the legal context, chain of custody is defined as the “chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical or electronic evidence.” This type of record helps establish that evidence is authentic, reliable, and substantially unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

Traditionally associated with physical evidence, chain of custody today applies equally to digital information. Proper documentation shows there were controls and safeguards in place continuously against alteration or loss of evidence. The documentation typically covers who had access, when, how it was stored, and how it moved between custodians or systems.

Modern custody of the evidence practices emphasize accountability, not just possession. Documentation that shows what controls were in place — such as locked storage for physical evidence or audit trails for electronic evidence — and whether handling procedures met reasonable standards helps establish integrity and allows a party to respond to tampering or contamination challenges. For electronic evidence, this may include controls around access permissions, audit trails, preservation measures, and defensible workflows that demonstrate responsible handling.

presidential election, the New York Post published a potentially election-altering news story 
about a years-long influence peddling scheme carried out by the family of the Democratic 
nominee for president, former Vice President Joe Biden.2 The Post article detailed how Hunter 
Biden leveraged his famous last name to provide foreign officials with access to his father in 
exchange for the Biden family’s significant financial gain.3 This information was recovered from 
the hard drive of a laptop attributed to Hunter Biden, and the article included pictures of a signed 
federal subpoena, demonstrating that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had seized that 
hard drive.4 Neither Hunter Biden nor the Biden presidential campaign denied the allegations or 
the provenance of the laptop; indeed, the Biden Department of Justice (DOJ) has since 
authenticated the laptop as evidence in federal court.5

origins.underlying_origin: **WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.

# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

S3:P12:P18.literal_quote:
Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

S9:P8:P8.literal_quote:
* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.

S9:P1:P7.literal_quote:
Reading Time — 8 minutes

March 26, 2026

Chain of custody, in the simplest of terms, is the chronological, documented record of everyone who has handled, accessed, or stored a piece of evidence. It serves as a “paper trail” that tracks the journey from the moment evidence is collected until it is presented in a legal proceeding. The purpose is to prove it has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

Such documentation is important to establish trust that the evidence is authentic and therefore admissible in court. The Federal Rules of Evidence govern the admissibility and authentication of evidence. Proper chain of custody helps convince the court there is a reasonable probability that the evidence is what the party claims it is, and is in substantially the same condition as when it was collected.

Without documentation showing who collected the evidence, when and where, who handled or accessed it, and how it was stored or transferred, opposing counsel may argue that it is unreliable or inadmissible, which can jeopardize the case.

Chain of custody documentation is a best practice for the handling of both physical and digital evidence.

## Key Takeaways for Legal Teams

S9:P8:P10.literal_quote:
* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.
* Courts evaluate custody to assess whether evidence was managed in a reasonably reliable and defensible manner, not whether handling was perfect.
* Breakdowns in the chain of custody can lead to admissibility challenges, adverse inference instructions, monetary sanctions, or other remedial measures.
* In ediscovery, consistency, traceability, and auditability are critical because if digital data is improperly duplicated, modified, or moved, it becomes harder to validate its authenticity.
* Defensible chain of custody is critical during discovery planning, where parties define how evidence will be handled so the approach can later be explained and justified.
* Strong custody practices allow legal teams to focus on substantive arguments rather than defending their processes under scrutiny.

## What Does Chain of Custody Mean in Legal Contexts?

In the legal context, chain of custody is defined as the “chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical or electronic evidence.” This type of record helps establish that evidence is authentic, reliable, and substantially unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

S9:P11:P12.literal_quote:
Traditionally associated with physical evidence, chain of custody today applies equally to digital information. Proper documentation shows there were controls and safeguards in place continuously against alteration or loss of evidence. The documentation typically covers who had access, when, how it was stored, and how it moved between custodians or systems.

Modern custody of the evidence practices emphasize accountability, not just possession. Documentation that shows what controls were in place — such as locked storage for physical evidence or audit trails for electronic evidence — and whether handling procedures met reasonable standards helps establish integrity and allows a party to respond to tampering or contamination challenges. For electronic evidence, this may include controls around access permissions, audit trails, preservation measures, and defensible workflows that demonstrate responsible handling.

S10:P1:P1.literal_quote: Chain of custody is the documented record of who collected, handled, transferred, examined, and stored evidence throughout an investigation.

presidential election, the New York Post published a potentially election-altering news story

Biden leveraged his famous last name to provide foreign officials with access to his father in

Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. U41.literal_quote:
# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

U42.literal_quote:
Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

**Editor's note:** *The Associated Press contributed to this article.*

U114.literal_quote: Chain of custody, in the simplest of terms, is the chronological, documented record of everyone who has handled, accessed, or stored a piece of evidence. It serves as a “paper trail” that tracks the journey from the moment evidence is collected until it is presented in a legal proceeding. The purpose is to prove it has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

U115.literal_quote: Such documentation is important to establish trust that the evidence is authentic and therefore admissible in court. The Federal Rules of Evidence govern the admissibility and authentication of evidence. Proper chain of custody helps convince the court there is a reasonable probability that the evidence is what the party claims it is, and is in substantially the same condition as when it was collected.

U116.literal_quote: Without documentation showing who collected the evidence, when and where, who handled or accessed it, and how it was stored or transferred, opposing counsel may argue that it is unreliable or inadmissible, which can jeopardize the case.

U117.literal_quote: Chain of custody documentation is a best practice for the handling of both physical and digital evidence.

U119.literal_quote:
* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.
* Courts evaluate custody to assess whether evidence was managed in a reasonably reliable and defensible manner, not whether handling was perfect.
* Breakdowns in the chain of custody can lead to admissibility challenges, adverse inference instructions, monetary sanctions, or other remedial measures.
* In ediscovery, consistency, traceability, and auditability are critical because if digital data is improperly duplicated, modified, or moved, it becomes harder to validate its authenticity.
* Defensible chain of custody is critical during discovery planning, where parties define how evidence will be handled so the approach can later be explained and justified.
* Strong custody practices allow legal teams to focus on substantive arguments rather than defending their processes under scrutiny.

U120.literal_quote: ## What Does Chain of Custody Mean in Legal Contexts?

U121.literal_quote: In the legal context, chain of custody is defined as the “chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical or electronic evidence.” This type of record helps establish that evidence is authentic, reliable, and substantially unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

U122.literal_quote: Traditionally associated with physical evidence, chain of custody today applies equally to digital information. Proper documentation shows there were controls and safeguards in place continuously against alteration or loss of evidence. The documentation typically covers who had access, when, how it was stored, and how it moved between custodians or systems.

U123.literal_quote: Modern custody of the evidence practices emphasize accountability, not just possession. Documentation that shows what controls were in place — such as locked storage for physical evidence or audit trails for electronic evidence — and whether handling procedures met reasonable standards helps establish integrity and allows a party to respond to tampering or contamination challenges. For electronic evidence, this may include controls around access permissions, audit trails, preservation measures, and defensible workflows that demonstrate responsible handling.

The purpose is to prove it has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

Such documentation is important to establish trust that the evidence is authentic and therefore admissible in court. The Federal Rules of Evidence govern the admissibility and authentication of evidence. Proper chain of custody helps convince the court there is a reasonable probability that the evidence is what the party claims it is, and is in substantially the same condition as when it was collected.

Without documentation showing who collected the evidence, when and where, who handled or accessed it, and how it was stored or transferred, opposing counsel may argue that it is unreliable or inadmissible, which can jeopardize the case.

Chain of custody documentation is a best practice for the handling of both physical and digital evidence.

## Key Takeaways for Legal Teams

U125.literal_quote:
* Chain of custody is a documented record that tracks how evidence is collected, handled, accessed, and preserved to prove its authenticity and integrity in court.
* Courts evaluate custody to assess whether evidence was managed in a reasonably reliable and defensible manner, not whether handling was perfect.
* Breakdowns in the chain of custody can lead to admissibility challenges, adverse inference instructions, monetary sanctions, or other remedial measures.
* In ediscovery, consistency, traceability, and auditability are critical because if digital data is improperly duplicated, modified, or moved, it becomes harder to validate its authenticity.
* Defensible chain of custody is critical during discovery planning, where parties define how evidence will be handled so the approach can later be explained and justified.
* Strong custody practices allow legal teams to focus on substantive arguments rather than defending their processes under scrutiny.

## What Does Chain of Custody Mean in Legal Contexts?

In the legal context, chain of custody is defined as the “chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody, control, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical or electronic evidence.” This type of record helps establish that evidence is authentic, reliable, and substantially unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

U126.literal_quote:
Traditionally associated with physical evidence, chain of custody today applies equally to digital information. Proper documentation shows there were controls and safeguards in place continuously against alteration or loss of evidence. The documentation typically covers who had access, when, how it was stored, and how it moved between custodians or systems.

Modern custody of the evidence practices emphasize accountability, not just possession. Documentation that shows what controls were in place — such as locked storage for physical evidence or audit trails for electronic evidence — and whether handling procedures met reasonable standards helps establish integrity and allows a party to respond to tampering or contamination challenges. For electronic evidence, this may include controls around access permissions, audit trails, preservation measures, and defensible workflows that demonstrate responsible handling.

presidential election, the New York Post published a potentially election-altering news story 
about a years-long influence peddling scheme carried out by the family of the Democratic 
nominee for president, former Vice President Joe Biden.2 The Post article detailed how Hunter 
Biden leveraged his famous last name to provide foreign officials with access to his father in 
exchange for the Biden family’s significant financial gain.3 This information was recovered from 
the hard drive of a laptop attributed to Hunter Biden, and the article included pictures of a signed 
federal subpoena, demonstrating that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had seized that 
hard drive.4 Neither Hunter Biden nor the Biden presidential campaign denied the allegations or 
the provenance of the laptop; indeed, the Biden Department of Justice (DOJ) has since 
authenticated the laptop as evidence in federal court.5

The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

**WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.

The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

# Testimony Reveals FBI Employees Who Warned Social Media Companies about Hack and Leak Operation Knew Hunter Biden Laptop Wasn’t Russian Disinformation

July 20, 2023

Press Release

**WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.  
  
The *Post* published its story early in the morning on October 14. That same day, representatives from the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force attended a previously scheduled meeting with Twitter, during which a Twitter employee asked the FITF about the authenticity of laptop. According to Section Chief Dehmlow’s testimony, an analyst in the FBI’s Criminal Investigative Division embedded in FITF began to respond that the laptop was real, when an FBI lawyer interrupted to say that the FBI had “no further comment,” regarding the laptop’s provenance:

Image

Later on October 14, FITF met with Facebook. During the FITF-Facebook meeting, Dehmlow responded to a similar question from a Facebook employee about Hunter Biden’s laptop by stating that the FBI, again, had “no comment.” The FBI made this decision despite being in possession of the laptop and having confirmed its authenticity. According to Dehmlow, multiple personnel on FITF knew that the laptop was real. She testified:

Image

   
In the hours following publication of the *Post*’s story, Twitter blocked the story from being shared, while Facebook deamplified the story, significantly reducing its circulation and prevalence in users’ newsfeeds. As the federal court in Missouri v. Biden explained in damning language, the FBI’s actions prevented millions of Americans from having a clear understanding about a salient issue in the 2020 presidential election:  
   
The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

\_\_\_\_\_  
  
**Editor's note:** *The Associated Press contributed to this article.*

At 5:00 a.m. ET, on Wednesday, October 14, 2020, less than three weeks before the 2020 
presidential election, the New York Post published a potentially election-altering news story 
about a years-long influence peddling scheme carried out by the family of the Democratic 
nominee for president, former Vice President Joe Biden.2 The Post article detailed how Hunter 
Biden leveraged his famous last name to provide foreign officials with access to his father in 
exchange for the Biden family’s significant financial gain.3 This information was recovered from 
the hard drive of a laptop attributed to Hunter Biden, and the article included pictures of a signed 
federal subpoena, demonstrating that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had seized that 
hard drive.4 Neither Hunter Biden nor the Biden presidential campaign denied the allegations or 
the provenance of the laptop; indeed, the Biden Department of Justice (DOJ) has since 
authenticated the laptop as evidence in federal court.5

**WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.

The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

Biden leveraged his famous last name to provide foreign officials with access to his father in 
exchange for the Biden family’s significant financial gain.3 This information was recovered from 
the hard drive of a laptop attributed to Hunter Biden, and the article included pictures of a signed 
federal subpoena, demonstrating that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had seized that 
hard drive.4 Neither Hunter Biden nor the Biden presidential campaign denied the allegations or 
the provenance of the laptop; indeed, the Biden Department of Justice (DOJ) has since

**WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.

The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.

# Ex-FBI officials charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden laptop probe

According to prosecutors, the Foreign Influence Task Force members’ false testimony to the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 prevented lawmakers from investigating further.

Ryan Knappenberger
/ October 23, 2026

Link copied

FILE - Deputy Assistant Director for Counterterrorism at the FBI Nikki Floris, testifies before the House Judiciary Committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, Oct. 22, 2019. (AP Photo/Susan Walsh, File)

WASHINGTON (CN) — The Justice Department charged two former FBI officials with lying to Congress Friday over their involvement in tax and money-laundering investigations into Hunter Biden in 2023.

Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former members of the now-disbanded Foreign Influence Task Force, were charged with making false statements to the House Judiciary Committee and surrendered to authorities.

If convicted, Floris and Benavides face up to eight years in prison.a

The case focuses on the FBI’s investigation into Hunter Biden’s laptop, acquired by the FBI on Dec. 9, 2019, which sparked conservative conspiracy theories that Joe Biden pressured Ukrainian officials while he was vice president to drop a corruption investigation into his son.

Floris served as deputy assistant director and functional head of the Foreign Influence Task Force from 2019-2022. Benavides was section chief from 2019 through the 2020 election. The Trump administration disbanded the task force in 2025.

The charges stem from a 2023 hearing before the House Judiciary Committee, where Floris and Benavides testified the task force was not involved in the FBI’s investigations into Biden. According to the DOJ, Floris told the committee she was not involved in any discussions about Biden as task force leader, while Benavides said he learned the FBI obtained Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia.

The Justice Department brought a criminal complaint against the two, a sign prosecutors have yet to present the case before a grand jury for an indictment. Grand juries in Washington have repeatedly rejected felony charges sought by the government in high-profile cases under the Trump administration.

In an initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui, Floris’ attorneys, Margaret Donovan and Mary Dohrmann, noted a criminal complaint is normally used if a defendant presents a flight risk or a danger to the community.

Faruqui noted it is uncommon for charges stemming from conduct nearly seven years ago to be brought via complaint rather than indictment. He scheduled a preliminary hearing for Tuesday.

The government claims in its affidavit that Floris and Benavides were “at the center” of the task force’s interactions with the FBI teams leading the probe into Biden. Prosecutors assert the two were tied to a 2019 analysis project referred to as “Round River,” which focused on the potential for Russian disinformation in the Hunter Biden probe.

The administration says Floris testified before the House Judiciary Committee on July 19, 2023, that she only had a “high-level” understanding of the probes and no involvement.

Benavides appeared before the committee on Sept. 28, 2023, according to prosecutors, when he similarly testified he had no knowledge of an investigation during his time on the task force.

# Testimony Reveals FBI Employees Who Warned Social Media Companies about Hack and Leak Operation Knew Hunter Biden Laptop Wasn’t Russian Disinformation

July 20, 2023

Press Release

**WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.  
  
The *Post* published its story early in the morning on October 14. That same day, representatives from the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force attended a previously scheduled meeting with Twitter, during which a Twitter employee asked the FITF about the authenticity of laptop. According to Section Chief Dehmlow’s testimony, an analyst in the FBI’s Criminal Investigative Division embedded in FITF began to respond that the laptop was real, when an FBI lawyer interrupted to say that the FBI had “no further comment,” regarding the laptop’s provenance:

Image

Later on October 14, FITF met with Facebook. During the FITF-Facebook meeting, Dehmlow responded to a similar question from a Facebook employee about Hunter Biden’s laptop by stating that the FBI, again, had “no comment.” The FBI made this decision despite being in possession of the laptop and having confirmed its authenticity. According to Dehmlow, multiple personnel on FITF knew that the laptop was real. She testified:

Image

   
In the hours following publication of the *Post*’s story, Twitter blocked the story from being shared, while Facebook deamplified the story, significantly reducing its circulation and prevalence in users’ newsfeeds. As the federal court in Missouri v. Biden explained in damning language, the FBI’s actions prevented millions of Americans from having a clear understanding about a salient issue in the 2020 presidential election:  
   
The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

# Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe

---

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:49 AM

4VIEW ALL PHOTOS

FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.

Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.

The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.

“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.

Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.

The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.

The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.

\_\_\_\_\_  
  
**Editor's note:** *The Associated Press contributed to this article.*

records.visible_text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Two former FBI officials were charged with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month's midterm contests.

Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, appeared in federal court Friday in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing to contest allegations their clients lied to lawmakers by saying that they did not participate in FBI investigations of Biden.

The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.

Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”

“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” her attorneys said in a statement. “It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”

Attorneys for Benavides accused the government of bringing “baseless criminal charges against him in a transparently political complaint.”

“This is another sad day for the Department of Justice,” his lawyers said in an emailed statement. “But now we are in court, and the truth will come out: Brad Benavides is a true patriot who devoted his career to protecting this country and its people. These charges are a disgrace.”

## A criminal complaint comes just before the midterms

The case was filed less than two weeks before the Nov. 3 elections via criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have not yet presented the allegations to a grand jury for an indictment. The Justice Department has repeatedly struggled in high-profile cases to convince grand juries in the nation’s capital to return indictments.

During the former FBI employees’ court appearance, both defense attorneys and the judge noted the unusual move to charge the case through a complaint, which is more often used by prosecutors when they have an urgent need to take people into custody because, for example, they present a danger or a risk of flight.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui remarked that it is “rare that we have charges this old coming in this nature," and over the objections of prosecutors who pushed for more time, set a preliminary hearing for next Tuesday, citing what he said was the “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants’ heads.

## The laptop discovery created turmoil in 2020 election

The revelation of the laptop’s existence in October 2020 injected a thorny storyline in the race between Trump, the Republican incumbent, and Biden’s father, Joe Biden, Trump’s Democratic challenger who went on to win the race.

WASHINGTON (CN) — The Justice Department charged two former FBI officials with lying to Congress Friday over their involvement in tax and money-laundering investigations into Hunter Biden in 2023.
